query: Ruby design patterns in sfl-engine codebase

claims.text: The codebase implements the NULL OBJECT pattern via Ports::Null module hierarchy (Null::Embedder, Null::ClauseStore, Null::Cache, Null::Breaker, Null::Instrumenter, Null::Logger, Null::Annotator) providing no-op implementations that allow Pipeline and other classes to work without concrete dependencies
claims.notes: All null objects include their corresponding Port module (e.g., Null::Embedder includes Ports::Embedder) and implement all required methods with no-op behavior. This is a classic Null Object pattern implementation.

claims.text: Ports::Null::Embedder implements the Embedder port interface with #embed returning [] and #embed_batch mapping over inputs, providing a safe default that prevents nil errors in Pipeline#embed_all

Pipeline class exhibits DEPENDENCY INJECTION pattern with nine constructor parameters (pass_one, pass_two, ideational_extractor, clause_store, embedding_store, embedder, cache, logger, instrumenter) all injected as dependencies, enabling easy testing and swapping of implementations
claims.notes: This is a pure DI pattern - all collaborators are injected via constructor, and default to Null implementations for optional dependencies. The class has no hardcoded dependencies on concrete implementations.

claims.text: Pipeline uses the DRY MONADS pattern via Dry::Monads[:result] to create a Result ladder where each stage (#parse, #pair_with_ideational, #annotate, #persist, #embed_all) returns Success/Failure and #bind short-circuits on Failure, eliminating explicit guard clauses between stages
claims.notes: The #compile method (lines 81-95) uses .bind to chain operations: parse().bind{...}.bind{...}.bind{...}.bind{...}. A failure at any stage automatically short-circuits the rest of the pipeline.

claims.text: Pipeline#compile implements a five-stage bind chain (parse -> pair_with_ideational -> annotate -> persist -> embed_all) where each stage returns Dry::Monads::Result and #bind only executes the next stage on Success, demonstrating the MONAD pattern for error propagation

LMFactory implements the FACTORY METHOD pattern with #for(task) method that creates and returns a DSPy::LM instance configured for a specific task (pass_two_annotation, pass_two_batch_annotation, etc.) based on per-task configuration resolved from the injected Config
claims.notes: The factory encapsulates the creation logic and resolves provider-specific API keys. It returns different LM instances for different tasks, all configured appropriately.

claims.text: EngineBuilder implements the BUILDER pattern with a class-level #call method that composes and returns a fully-configured Engine instance by assembling its dependencies: ClauseAnnotator, BatchClauseAnnotator, breaker, instrumenter, and logger, each properly configured with their own dependencies
claims.notes: EngineBuilder.create is a classic builder that handles the complex construction of an Engine with all its properly wired dependencies, shielding callers from the construction complexity.

claims.text: Core::Ports module implements the ADAPTER pattern by defining abstract interfaces (Embedder, ClauseStore, Cache, Breaker, Instrumenter, SyntacticParser) that concrete implementations must satisfy, allowing different implementations to be swapped without changing client code
claims.notes: Each port module (e.g., Ports::Embedder) defines the interface with abstract methods that raise NotImplementedError. Concrete adapters like PgEmbeddingStore or LLM::Embedder implement these interfaces.

claims.text: LLM::Embedder implements the Ports::Embedder adapter interface by providing concrete #embed and #embed_batch methods that delegate to RubyLLM's embedding functionality, adapting the external LLM library to the internal port contract

Store::PgClauseStore implements the Ports::ClauseStore adapter interface with concrete PostgreSQL-based implementations of #replace_document, #find_by_document, #find, and #list, adapting database operations to the clause storage port contract
claims.notes: PgClauseStore includes Ports::ClauseStore (line 32) and provides PostgreSQL-specific implementations. This is the Repository pattern combined with Adapter pattern.

claims.text: PassOne::Engine demonstrates the STRATEGY pattern by delegating syntactic parsing to an injected SyntacticParser port (SpacySidecarParser in production, Null/Fake in tests), allowing the parsing algorithm to be swapped without changing the Engine class
claims.notes: The parser is injected via constructor (line 12), and Engine#process delegates to parser.parse (line 41). Different parsers can be injected for different use cases.

claims.text: LLM::Engine uses the STRATEGY pattern with clause_annotator and batch_clause_annotator as interchangeable annotation strategies, allowing different annotation approaches (single vs batch) to be selected at runtime based on context

Store::PgClauseStore implements the REPOSITORY pattern by encapsulating all database operations for clauses (CRUD operations on clauses, ideational_payloads, interpersonal_payloads tables) behind a simple interface (#replace_document, #find_by_document, #find, #list), hiding the persistence details from the domain layer
claims.notes: The repository handles transactions (line 43-46), complex joins, and reconstruction of domain objects from database rows, completely hiding Sequelize/PostgreSQL details from callers.

claims.text: Core::Ports::TimeoutBreaker implements the CIRCUIT BREAKER pattern with a single timeout ownership model, wrapping calls with Timeout.timeout to prevent cascading failures and enforce time limits on external service calls (LLM annotations)
claims.notes: The implementation notes (lines 14-19) explicitly state this is deliberately not a full circuit breaker with failure counting, but a minimal adapter with single timeout ownership. It includes Ports::Breaker (line 21).

claims.text: Pipeline class implements the COMPOSITE pattern by composing multiple processing stages (parse, pair_with_ideational, annotate, persist, embed_all) into a single #compile operation, treating the pipeline as a tree of operations where each stage can itself be a complex operation
claims.notes: The pipeline composes stages using dry-monads Result ladder, where each stage is a node that can be composed with others. The class comment (lines 9-14) explicitly describes this composition.

claims.text: The codebase follows HEXAGONAL ARCHITECTURE (Ports & Adapters) with Core::Ports defining the domain interfaces and concrete implementations in lib/sfl/llm/, lib/sfl/store/pg_*, and lib/sfl/core/pass_one/ providing the adapters that connect external systems to the domain, keeping the domain logic independent of infrastructure concerns
claims.notes: This is evident from the directory structure: ports define interfaces, store/ has pg_* adapters for PostgreSQL, llm/ has adapters for LLM providers, core/pass_one/ has parsing adapters, and core/pipeline.rb is the domain composition point.

claims.text: Boot module serves as the COMPOSITION ROOT (Dependency Injection container) where all ENV configuration is read and all top-level dependencies are wired together, with the explicit constraint that it is the ONLY place in the codebase that reads ENV (line 7-13 comment)
claims.notes: Boot.call (line 141-166) is the single entry point that reads ENV via Dotenv.load, builds LLM collaborators, configures tracing, connects DB, and returns a Result with all wired dependencies. All other classes receive config via constructor injection.

claims.text: The instrumenter ports (Ports::Instrumenter, Null::Instrumenter) follow a DECORATOR-like pattern where instrumentation can be added around operations without modifying the operations themselves, as seen in Pipeline#annotate_all which wraps pass_two.annotate_batch with instrumenter.instrument
claims.notes: The instrumentation is wrapped around the actual operation (lines 133-135), allowing behavior to be added without modifying the core logic. This is decorator-adjacent but not a pure decorator pattern.

claims.text: Pipeline#compile follows a TEMPLATE METHOD pattern with a fixed sequence of steps (parse -> pair_with_ideational -> annotate -> persist -> embed_all) that cannot be reordered but can be optionally skipped via parameters (pass_one_only, store, embed, resume)
claims.notes: The method defines a skeleton algorithm with fixed step ordering, but some steps can be conditionally executed based on parameters. This is similar to Template Method but with more flexibility.

claims.text: Pipeline#annotate_with_cache implements a CHAIN OF RESPONSIBILITY-like pattern where it first tries the cache (hits), then falls back to fresh annotation (misses), with self-healing logic that treats untrusted cache entries as misses, creating a responsibility chain: cache -> validation -> fresh computation
claims.notes: Lines 146-153 show the chain: partition cache, filter for trusted hits, treat untrusted as misses, then fresh_annotations for misses. This creates a handling chain.

critique_claims.text: No explicit Proxy pattern implementation found - while there are adapter implementations, a true Proxy (controlling access to another object) is not evident in the current codebase structure
critique_claims.notes: The legacy codebase mentioned SafeOpenAIClientProxy but this was explicitly not ported (Boot.rb line 29-34 comment). The current architecture uses adapters and DI rather than proxies.

critique_claims.text: Observer pattern is not explicitly used - while there are callback parameters (on_progress, on_turn_start, stop_requested) in Analysis::Engine, these are simple function callbacks rather than a full Observer pattern with Subject/Observer hierarchy
critique_claims.notes: The callbacks (lines 59-61) are injected as simple procs/lambdas, not as Observer objects with subscribe/notify methods.

critique_claims.text: The distinction between Factory (LMFactory creates individual LMs) and Builder (EngineBuilder composes an Engine from multiple components) patterns is well-executed, but there may be opportunities to consolidate some factory-like code in Boot#build_llm_config which has multiple similar task config constructions
critique_claims.notes: Lines 195-222 show multiple similar task_config_from_env calls that could potentially be refactored into a more declarative configuration if the number of tasks grows significantly.
